title: Aurum is a scam
author: Aggressive-pingpong
selftext:
Aurum Foundation is a Ponzi scheme. That means there is no real product generating the promised returns. The money you deposit doesn't get traded by any AI. It sits in a pool, and when you get paid, you're being paid with money deposited by the person who signed up after you. It works as long as new people keep joining. The moment recruitment slows down, withdrawals stop and everyone loses everything. This is one of the oldest financial frauds in existence, just dressed up with new technology to look legitimate.

Here's how Aurum does it. They tell you their AI bot will trade your crypto and return 30% every single month. To put that in perspective: the most successful trading fund ever built, run by some of the smartest mathematicians on the planet, averaged 66% per year. Aurum is promising that every 30 days, to anyone who signs up online, with no experience required. It is mathematically impossible.

Here's the proof. Someone went undercover on one of their internal recruiting Zoom calls. Their own executive never once used the word "investment." He called it "referral marketing" and coached recruiters to avoid explaining how the bot actually works, because in his exact words, "it's unknown to me, it's unknown to you." They don't know how it works because there is no bot. There's just your money going in.

And when people try to take their money out? First they're told to wait 72 hours. Then withdrawals become quarterly. Then a 12% "compliance fee" appears, which you have to pay to access your own funds. Regulators in five countries, Russia, Nigeria, Italy, New Zealand, and Hong Kong, have already warned the public about this platform.
